teams.heading: Fiji's 21-16 victims Italy lose Miotti and Ferrari for Twickenham rematch
teams.body: Fiji meet Italy again at Twickenham in a match that settles 11th and 12th place in the Nations Championship, and the Azzurri must reshuffle at fly-half. Domingo Miotti, who left the field in the 48th minute in Udine, has a left hamstring injury and returns to Montpellier for rehabilitation. Prop Simone Ferrari withdrew an hour before kick-off with a left upper-limb injury and goes back to Treviso. Italy do welcome back Lynagh. Centre Leonardo Marin admitted his side conceded too many stupid penalties in the second half.

lead.why: It is fresh, hard news on Fiji's next opponent for the Twickenham rematch, not a rerun of the Udine win.

teams.heading: Guardian's Robert Kitson hails England's champagne rugby after 37-12 All Blacks win
teams.body: Kitson's Guardian verdict credited England and Ireland with the northern hemisphere's champagne rugby in the round that tees up finals weekend, and Saturday's 37-12 win over New Zealand was England's contribution. Ben Earl was man of the match in a five-try display that brought a fifth consecutive Test victory and back-to-back wins over the All Blacks for the first time since 2002 and 2003. Of the 46 fans in the app who answered, 96% were buzzing at the result.

teams.heading: Thomas Ramos recalled to France squad for Nations Championship final against Springboks
teams.body: Fabien Galthié has brought the Toulouse full-back back into his 42-man group after two months out with a thigh muscle injury and a relapse. Rugbyrama expects France's record points scorer to go straight into the starting XV at Twickenham, as Matthieu Jalibert did after a similar setback. That would return Théo Attissogbe, shifted to 15 in Ramos's absence, to the wing opposite Bielle-Biarrey, restoring the back three from the last Six Nations. It also adds a leading voice, with Grégory Alldritt forced out of the squad.

lead.why: A fresh France selection event: the record points scorer's recall reshapes the back three before the final.

teams.heading: Ireland meet Australia in third-v-third finals clash after 20-17 Springbok win
teams.body: The inaugural Nations Championship finals weekend pairs Farrell's side with the Wallabies, with every match staged at Allianz Stadium, Twickenham. There is more than placing at stake. Each of the first five matches earns a point for the winner's hemisphere, and the final between France and South Africa is worth two. The Guardian's Robert Kitson paired the 20-17 defeat of the world champion Springboks with England's 37-12 win over the All Blacks as another resounding northern-hemisphere double.

lead.why: It confirms Ireland's opponent and stakes for finals weekend, the freshest hard news about the senior side.

teams.heading: Italy lose Miotti and Ferrari to injury after 16-21 Fiji defeat
teams.body: Domingo Miotti, lively until he left the field in the 48th minute of Saturday's 16-21 defeat by Fiji in Udine, has a left hamstring injury, according to Italy's medical staff. Simone Ferrari, named in the matchday squad, withdrew an hour before kick-off with a left upper-limb injury, Marco Riccioni taking his place. Both will have scans in camp and then return to their clubs — Miotti to Montpellier, Ferrari to Treviso — with rehabilitation run jointly with the national team's staff.

lead.why: A fresh injury bulletin ruling two Italy starters out of camp is new hard news on the senior side.

teams.heading: Gregor Townsend's 10 changes pay off as Scotland rout Japan 67-5
teams.body: Scotland's 67-5 win over Japan at Murrayfield on Saturday came from a heavily rotated side. Townsend made 10 changes after the narrow 15-12 victory over Australia, resting much of his first-choice team with, in Rugby World's reading, one eye on finals weekend. Tom Jordan started at 10 in place of Finn Russell, and the reshaped XV led 29-0 at half-time before running in 11 tries against Eddie Jones' weakened Brave Blossoms.

lead.why: McConnell, the U20 win and the captaincy switch have all run; Townsend's 10-change rotation against Japan is the remaining Scotland angle.

teams.heading: Steve Tandy vows Wales rotation for Japan play-off after 26-29 Australia loss
teams.body: Tandy doubled down after the game on Saturday night: "I can rotate the team and we'll still put in a performance. It doesn't matter who wears the shirt, we've got to perform." Eleven players started against Japan, New Zealand and Australia, so this weekend's 9th/10th play-off against the Brave Blossoms at Twickenham's Allianz Stadium offers a rare look at depth. Alex Cuthbert wants the frontline kept on; Japan, stretched by injury, conceded 24 tries losing to England and Scotland.

lead.why: Tandy's confirmed plan to rotate for the Japan play-off is the freshest Wales selection news; the Botham row and the Australia result have already run.

teams.heading: Delguy and Wenger forced off as Vivas red card sinks Pumas 45-17
teams.body: Argentina's 45-17 loss to France at the Stade de France came at a cost. Bautista Delguy and Boris Wenger went off early and did not return, after Santiago Chocobares had withdrawn hours before kick-off, with Justo Piccardo starting at inside centre. The Pumas led 10-7 before trailing 14-10 at the break. Hollie Davidson's yellow for Mayco Vivas was upgraded to red, Julián Montoya was then sin-binned, and France cashed in with three tries. Scotland await in the battle for seventh.

lead.why: The only NEW item, #1, is a France hooker's interview marked as another team's story, so the Pumas' own defeat, with its injuries and red card, stays the lead.

teams.heading: Len Ikitau backs Wallabies defence after man-of-the-match display in 29-26 win
teams.body: A try, an assist and a match-high 15 carries in Cardiff capped a stop-start year for the 2025 John Eales Medal winner. Shoulder surgery, an ankle injury against South Africa and a concussion that wrecked his Bledisloe Cup hopes all interrupted it. Ikitau credited the system under new defence coach Scott McLeod: "defensively, we've taken a step up." Ireland, Friday's fifth-place play-off opponents at Twickenham, may be without Dan Sheehan, whose yellow card against South Africa was upgraded to red.

lead.why: The freshest story about the Wallabies themselves: their man of the match backing the new defence before the Ireland play-off.

teams.heading: Japan's Eddie Jones hailed Townsend's Scotland two days before 67-5 rout
teams.body: Japan's coach had talked up the opposition before last Saturday's Nations Championship meeting, and Scotland then put 11 tries past his side in a 67-5 win at Murrayfield. Speaking on the Thursday, Jones said: “Gregor’s done a great job, and I think Scotland should be grateful for the job that he’s done.” He argued Scotland were performing well for a country with two professional teams to pick from. Takuro Matsunaga scored Japan's only try — in the second half — after the hosts led 29-0 at the break.

lead.why: The Murrayfield result and team selection have already run, so Jones' unreported pre-match verdict on Townsend is the remaining Japan item and has to be read against the 67-5 outcome.

teams.heading: Jeff Wilson says All Blacks 'had no energy' in 37-12 England loss
teams.body: Former wing Jeff Wilson, speaking on The Breakdown, said the side looked physically and emotionally drained at Twickenham and "just looked as though they were done." The defeat was New Zealand's fifth Test loss of the season, the most since 1998, and came a week after their first defeat to Wales since 1953. Wilson missed Ruben Love's combination with Damian McKenzie but argued there was enough talent on the field, and that some reputations had been dented. England await in the third-place playoff.

lead.why: The board-backing-Rennie story ran yesterday, so Jeff Wilson's verdict on the England loss is the strongest new All Blacks item.

teams.heading: Marco van Staden likely banned for France final, several Springboks doubtful
teams.body: Rugbyrama expects the Springboks to go into Sunday's Nations Championship final against France at Twickenham diminished, with Marco van Staden probably suspended and several senior players uncertain; the French outlet does not say what the ban relates to. Damian Willemse was forced off early in Saturday's 20-17 defeat by Ireland in Dublin, and former prop Steven Kitshoff has pointed to "the couple of injuries that we had over the weekend." Jasper Wiese is already serving a four-match ban for a red card against France.

lead.why: A probable suspension and several fitness doubts before the final is the only fresh hard team news about the Springboks.
